text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Financial services group Fortis tries to calm bankers at its subsidiary MeesPierson. (p1)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM's president Pieter Bouw announces during annual earnings presentation that he will resign. (p1)
- Amsterdam AEX jumps above the 800 mark on news of Fed decision not to increase rates. (p1)
- New York Stock Exchange happy with ABN AMRO bank's listing. (p1)
- Cabinet hastens to introduce new bill on corporate splits. (p1)
- ABN AMRO and Goldman Sachs chosen as syndicate leaders for one billion dollar loan for Russia's Gazprom GAZP.RTS. (p3)
- Harbour company HES Beheer announces claims issue to improve its bad financial situation. (p3)
- Transport company Nedlloyd posts a 45 million guilder Q1 loss: company expects positive full year results. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- Coalition agrees on forming city provinces in Rotterdam and Eindhoven. (p2)
- OECD praises the Netherlands and itself for tackling unemployment. (p2)
- KLM books 236 million guilder net profit in 1996/1997 book year solely because of its partner Northwest Airlines. (p2)
- Price of Vendex temporary employment agency unit Vedior's share isssue set between 33 and 37 guilders. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Professor D. Wolfson of the government's scientific body WRR forecasts pay increases due to shortage of staff after year 2000. (p1)
- Reorganisation at KPN's PTT Telecom unit will cost some 1,100 jobs. (p33)
- Dutch market for mortgages continues to grow. (p35)
- Automation company Baan mulls a separate listing for its Baan Business Systems. (p37)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Engineering company Heidemij books 10 percent higher Q1 net at 4.5 million guilders. (p10)
- Dutch exporters to Japan complain about lack of cooperation from economic affairs ministry. (p11)
TROUW
- Rules against milk lake remain unchanged until 2005. (p5)
- Science publisher E.J. Brill seeks bourse listing (p7)
